crate_layout:
Single binary crate `wrangler` (edition 2021), replacing the bash-glue + python-curses runtime with one multi-call executable dispatched by argv[1] (sidebar | toggle | spawn | focus | hook | install-hooks | tmux-entry). Backend is ratatui + crossterm (already vendored in prototype/Cargo.lock), NOT curses -- every curses-specific behavior in the specs maps onto a crossterm equivalent. Suggested tree:

src/main.rs -- subcommand dispatch (thin); resolves SIDEBAR_PANE from $TMUX_PANE and STATE_DIR from $XDG_STATE_HOME|~/.local/state for the modes that need them.

src/model.rs (NEW, not in specs) -- shared domain types the pure band all reference: Window, Pane, PaneId, AgentSession/Session, Row + RowKey (Window/AgentWindow/Pane/Agent{id,pane}), Indicator + ProgressState + StateColor, StatePaths, Cached snapshot, and the loop-resident state structs (LabelCache, WidthState, LoopState). Must exist first so workflow-2 modules compile and fixture-test in isolation.

src/proto.rs -- wire formats: registry-record serialize/parse (rstrip-\n-only, 2/4/5-field dispatch + legacy back-compat), marker read/write, selection tab-framing, record_key/session_id_from_key, parse_field_int (ASCII-isdigit gate), ns token minting, and the flock-guarded claim_attention / prune_notified_flags. Pure serialize/parse/normalize/field-int split into a submodule for fixture tests; fs/flock kept as thin wrappers.

src/color.rs (spec path src/client/color.rs) -- palette tables (MUTED/SATURATED/BRIGHT, ANSI base, base-UI + indicator pair ids), rgb_to_ansi256, read_theme, theme_palette, agent_pair_for, indicator_pair_for. init_agent_colors is the terminal-side pair allocator (integration, not fixturable).

src/labels.rs -- yaml_scalar, workspace_field, scan_tail, agent_label, label_mode_from (pure core) + the mtime-keyed sticky Claude/Copilot session_meta caches.

src/tmux.rs -- run_tmux choke point (swallows every error -> empty string, never propagates), fetch_windows, window_real_panes, strip_status_prefix, focus/activate, and the spawn-race self-exit numeric %N comparison.

src/hook.rs -- agent-hook port: parse_payload, sanitize_session_id, normalize_event, find_agent_pid (bounded ps ancestry), register/refresh/ensure_registered, mark_working/mark_attention (mutually-exclusive markers), end_session. Writes the on-disk contract that assoc/notify/rows read.

src/daemon/ (the sidebar-process modules, all consuming tmux + proto):
  mod.rs   -- run/run_loop/poll_step/check_self_exit/build_and_reconcile/compute_dirty_and_draw + FocusGuard (mode-1004). The event-loop + model-build owner.
  rows.rs  -- build_rows, append_agent_rows, indicator_for + Indicator::resolve, spinner_frame, fit (pure:true, 126 fixtures).
  assoc.rs -- ppid_map, process_under, parse_registry_record, fetch_agent_sessions (two-pass), attention_token, pid_alive, strip_status_prefix.
  notify.rs-- attention_token, client_ttys, claim_attention, acknowledge_focused_attention, notify_attention, write_tty.
  width.rs -- min_width/sync_width_enabled/read_width/write_width + WidthSync{new,poll} state machine.

src/client/mod.rs -- the paint half: draw, render_line, row_style, fit, read/write_selection, TerminalGuard (raw/alt-screen/mouse/focus setup+RAII teardown), set_focus_reporting. Splits cleanly from daemon only if the logical daemon(semantic Indicator)/client(spinner_frame+fit at paint) boundary is honored.

src/glue/{mod.rs, install_hooks.rs, tmux_cmd.rs} -- tmux-entry (init: bind keys, hooks, automatic-rename-format patch), toggle/spawn/focus subcommands, and the hooks-manifest-driven installer (atomic_write, dumps with ensure_ascii, install_claude/install_copilot, ordered manifest). hooks-manifest.json embedded or shipped as data.

Test wiring: a fixtures harness that loads prototype/spec/fixtures/{color,labels,assoc,rows}.json (342/72/63/126 cases) and drives the pure functions; integration tests for the not_fixturable set (tmux/ps stubs on PATH, temp STATE_DIR, mtime-bump sequences, flock double-fire) live behind #[cfg(test)] with a fake-tmux and fake-ps shim.

build_order.rationale: NEW shared-types module the specs assume but never home. Window/Pane/AgentSession/Row/RowKey/Indicator/ProgressState/StatePaths/Cached and the loop/label/width state structs. Nothing behavioral; must land first so the pure band (rows especially, which needs assoc/labels/color TYPES) can compile and be fixture-tested independently. No fixtures of its own.

Foundational wire formats every other module reads/writes. Pure core (serialize/parse_record, normalize_event, parse_field_int, key framing, read_attention_token) is fixture-testable with no tmux/terminal. The fs/flock wrappers (marker write, claim_attention) are thin std::fs and can be exercised by temp-dir integration tests; keep them isolated. Build early because assoc/notify/hook/rows/width/client all depend on its byte-exact framing.

342 golden fixtures. rgb_to_ansi256, theme_palette, read_theme, agent_pair_for, indicator_pair_for are pure math + one settings.json read. Only init_agent_colors (curses pair allocation) is integration and is deferred to the terminal-setup step. Parallelizable with proto/labels/rows.

72 fixtures. yaml_scalar/workspace_field/scan_tail/agent_label/label_mode_from are pure and leaf (json+fs-read only). The mtime-keyed sticky caches are stateful but wrap the pure core; their stickiness is verified in integration. Parallelizable with proto/color/rows.

Marked pure:true, 126 fixtures. build_rows/indicator_for/Indicator::resolve/spinner_frame/fit/append_agent_rows are pure given hand-built inputs. Needs only the TYPES from model/assoc/labels/color, not their runtime behavior, so it parallelizes once model.rs lands. The daemon/client semantic-vs-painted split lives here and must be nailed before the loop is wired.

Integration substrate: run_tmux subprocess choke point + fetch_windows produce the Window/Pane data every daemon module consumes. Must swallow all errors to empty string (control-flow-load-bearing). First of the sequential band; assoc/width/notify/glue/daemon all sit on it. fetch_windows is not fixturable (shells to tmux).

The write side of the on-disk contract (registry + markers), plus ps ancestry walk and stdin/env IO. Depends only on proto framing, so it can begin as soon as proto lands and run in parallel with the tmux stack, but it is integration (fs mutation, ps, TMUX_PANE) so it sits in the sequential band. Its byte output must round-trip through assoc/proto parse fixtures.

Two-pass association: shells to `ps` (ppid_map) and `tmux list-panes -a`, reads REGISTRY + markers, and does DESTRUCTIVE prune. Order-sensitive (sorted listdir). Depends on labels + color + tmux + proto. process_under/parse_registry_record/strip_status_prefix/scan_tail bits are fixtured (63 cases); the fetch_agent_sessions orchestration is integration-only.

Width state machine issuing tmux resize-pane and read/write of the shared width file. Sticky per-process state (floor/sync/pending_width/relayout_grace). Depends on tmux; the trickiest reconciliation logic. Needs a live-ish tmux + resize sequence to verify; not fixturable.

flock cross-process dedup, tty/OSC writes, tmux subprocess round-trips. Depends on tmux + assoc + proto. claim_attention/attention_token are shared with proto (dedup to one home). Requires a multi-instance + focus-race integration harness; strict '>' token semantics and blocking LOCK_EX are the parity core.

toggle/spawn/focus subcommands, tmux-entry init, and the hooks-manifest installer (atomic_write, ensure_ascii JSON, ordered keys, shlex.quote parity, all-or-nothing group replacement). Depends on tmux + hook + width (shared width-file delete) + the daemon spawn command. Byte-exact JSON output is an idempotency contract; integration-tested against golden config diffs.

Top-level integrator: the fixed-cadence event loop, poll_step, self-exit checks, build gating, dirty-diff repaint, FocusGuard. Wires rows/color/assoc/notify/width/tmux/proto together and owns the sticky loop state + deep-equality snapshot diff. Built last-but-one; the whole stack must exist. Note: overlaps the client run-loop spec -- resolve to one home (see risks).

The paint half + terminal lifecycle (ratatui/crossterm TerminalGuard, mouse, mode-1004), draw/render_line/row_style/fit, shared-selection read/write. Merges with daemon into the single sidebar process; the daemon(semantic)/client(painted) split from the rows spec is the boundary to preserve. Built alongside daemon as the final deliverable; verified by running the real sidebar in tmux.

risks: OWNERSHIP OVERLAP daemon/mod.rs vs client/mod.rs: both specs describe the run loop (run_loop/run_sidebar), poll, self_exit, focus, activate, width_sync, fit, set_focus_reporting. This is a logical daemon(build semantic rows)/client(resolve spinner+paint) split within ONE process, NOT two processes (the rows spec confirms: daemon emits semantic Indicator, client resolves spinner_frame/fit at paint). Decide the single home for each duplicated fn BEFORE coding or you double-implement and drift.

SHARED claim_attention/attention_token DEFINED 3x: proto, notify, and assoc each spec an attention_token, and claim_attention appears in both proto and notify. Pick ONE implementation and ONE integer width (i128 recommended) used across attention_token/claim_attention/acknowledge_focused_attention, or dedup/equality/ordering silently diverges. Token domain mixes small monotonic ns-tokens with legacy st_mtime_ns fallbacks compared by plain integer <= .

SHARED DOMAIN TYPES HAVE NO HOME: rows (pure) needs AgentSession/Window/Row/Indicator; assoc/labels/color produce them. The specs never assign these a module. Without a src/model.rs defined up front the workflow-2 parallel band cannot compile or fixture-test independently. This is the single biggest sequencing blocker.

CURSES -> RATATUI/CROSSTERM TRANSLATION: specs are written against curses. Riskiest reproductions: the COLORS>=256 palette gate (must read terminfo max_colors the same way), init_pair background -1 / use_default_colors (default-color transparency), init_pair-failure `continue` skip-without-advancing-id, mouseinterval(0) immediate button-down, and mode-1004 raw-fd writes bypassing the screen buffer. Plus a DELIBERATE divergence flagged in the client spec: crossterm FocusGained/FocusLost must be a wake/redraw trigger ONLY and must NOT set has_focus (has_focus is a tmux fact = active pane of active window), contradicting the prototype which sets it from the crossterm event.

PYTHON STRING/NUMERIC SEMANTICS: str.isdigit() (reject '', '-5', '+5', '24px', whitespace; gate on non-empty ASCII 0-9 runs, never str::parse), str.split()/split_whitespace vs split(' '), str.splitlines() (many unicode boundaries, drops trailing empty) vs Rust lines(), str.isalnum() (strip_status_prefix) unicode breadth, and round() banker's-vs-half-away in rgb_to_ansi256 (provably no exact-half input but round-half-to-even defensively; verify (202,138,4)->178 gold + a full 0..255 sweep).

FRAMING BYTE-EXACTNESS (#1 back-compat trap): registry records and selection strip ONLY trailing '\n' (never tabs/spaces) to preserve the empty leading pane field of pane-less/daemon records and the empty trailing transcript field; single-value token markers use full strip(). 5-field TAB layout with genuine empty fields; legacy 2-field accepted (agent forced 'claude', empty pid = trusted); 3-field REJECTED (skip, not prune); >=5 truncated to 5. A trimming reader shifts every field left and the record gets pruned.

STICKY STATE MUST BE OWNED, NOT RECOMPUTED: label caches (is_custom + mtime keys, keep-previous-on-empty), color _agent_color_pairs (allocated once at startup), width (floor/sync cached once, pending_width/relayout_grace/last_pane_set), and the loop (cached 7-tuple, last_painted, animating, selected_key, offset). Redraw gating is DEEP structural PartialEq over the whole cached snapshot+selection (has_focus is inside it) -- a shallow/identity compare busy-repaints or misses data changes. build_rows runs only on poll or (frame-advance && animating), where animating derives from the PREVIOUS build.

MTIME KEY MISMATCH BY DESIGN: Claude session_meta uses float getmtime(seconds) with exact-equality; Copilot title uses st_mtime_ns(int); marker/notified tokens use st_mtime_ns fallback. Keep them DISTINCT types, compare exactly, and use true nanoseconds (tv_sec*1e9+tv_nsec), never seconds*1e9. Unifying the timestamp type changes re-scan/dedup cadence.

DETERMINISTIC ITERATION ORDER: sorted(os.listdir) registry order drives candidate/row order + title-collision tiebreak; tmux list-windows/list-panes emission order drives the pane tree (last-child branch glyph) and pane_owner; notify_attention representative map + fire loop rely on insertion order; agent sections are sorted(set(names)) dedup-then-sort. Use ordered Vec / IndexMap everywhere, HashSet only for `sidebars`. A HashMap makes ambiguous placements and notifications nondeterministic.

run_tmux MUST FAIL SOFT: non-zero exit and stderr discarded, return stdout-or-empty, never propagate. A dead server yields "" and callers degrade (self-exit on no windows). Any `?`/unwrap/Command::status().success() diverges and changes control flow. Same best-effort swallow applies to every tty write, resize-pane, and notification -- an error escaping into the poll loop kills the sidebar (parity break).

NUMERIC PANE-ID COMPARISON: spawn-race tiebreak strips the leading '%' and compares as integers (int(p[1:]) < int(SIDEBAR_PANE[1:])); lexical string compare ('%10' < '%9') picks the wrong survivor and breaks one-sidebar-per-window. Pane ids stay opaque strings everywhere else.

INSTALLER JSON PARITY: json.dumps ensure_ascii escapes all non-ASCII as \uXXXX (serde_json does NOT by default -> must force), 2-space indent + exactly one trailing newline, INSERTION-ordered keys (preserve_order/IndexMap), shlex.quote reproduced byte-for-byte, all-or-nothing wrangler group replacement via a loose \bagent-hook\.sh\b.*\b<agent>\b regex, per-format file modes (claude 0600 + always-rewritten .wrangler.bak backup; copilot 0644, no backup), and same-directory atomic rename with chmod-before-rename. Any drift breaks idempotency and produces spurious config diffs.

UNKNOWN: is there a real daemon process or is 'daemon' just the sidebar process's build-side modules? The module tree (rows/assoc/notify/width under src/daemon/) plus a spawned-per-window sidebar suggests NO separate daemon -- 'daemon' = the sidebar process's model layer, 'client' = its paint layer, one process. Confirm before wiring notify's cross-instance flock arbitration (spec hints a single owner COULD replace flock with an in-process mutex, but only if there is genuinely one process coordinating -- there is not; there is one sidebar per window, so flock/LOCK_EX must stay).
